about.title: Moraga Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens on a corridor like Moraga Way or Street Marys Road, the family left behind is often left with more questions than answers. Contra Costa County's public crash records for Moraga show injury collisions occur here, and while recent counts have shown zero traffic deaths, any fatal incident carries the same weight for the people left grieving. California wrongful death law limits who can bring a claim, sets a two-year deadline from the date of death, and allows recovery for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. This is a civil matter, entirely separate from any criminal proceedings that might follow. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect Moraga families with an independent attorney who can walk through eligibility, deadlines, and next steps at no upfront cost, so you can focus on your family first.

items.title: Standing Rules Are Followed Carefully
items.desc: California law limits who may file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney in our network can help sort out who qualifies before any filing decisions are made.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Taken Seriously
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California must generally be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, may be involved. Missing this deadline can end a claim entirely, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can explain how these categories might apply to your specific loss.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Moraga?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. An attorney can review your family's situation to determine who is eligible to bring the claim.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after losing a family member?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That deadline is much shorter if the claim involves a government entity, such as a public agency responsible for a road like Moraga Road or Canyon Road. Because deadlines can be easy to miss during a difficult time, it helps to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: Does this cost anything to explore?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You can ask questions and understand your options before committing to anything.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A wrongful death claim is a civil action pursued by the family to recover losses like funeral costs and lost support, while any criminal case is handled independently by prosecutors and doesn't determine the outcome of a civil claim.
